subject.title: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot anthropic-messages transport silently hangs ~365s in isolated cron sessions (2026.5.27)

question: Should OpenClaw treat provider watchdog aborts with no assistant text, no tool lifecycle, and no message-tool delivery as fallback-safe for GitHub Copilot Claude `anthropic-messages` cron runs?
rationale: The code can be changed narrowly, but the permanent behavior decides whether an aborted agent run may be retried on another model; that affects side-effect safety and provider default behavior.

options.title: Approve guarded fallback policy
options.body: Classify aborted no-output results as fallback-worthy only when no tool, subagent, or message delivery evidence exists, and require live Copilot proof before closing.

options.title: Transport-only recovery first
options.body: Add a Copilot Anthropic first-token idle timeout or heartbeat mechanism and keep aborted embedded results fail-closed until transport evidence is clearer.

options.title: Keep fail-closed
options.body: Continue surfacing the run as a cron error and document switching the primary away from Copilot Claude when the transport hangs.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded fallback policy
recommendation.body: Classify aborted no-output results as fallback-worthy only when no tool, subagent, or message delivery evidence exists, and require live Copilot proof before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history across the Copilot provider routing, stream wrapper, and agent-runtime fallback surfaces involved in this decision.
